Elegoo Mars 2P · source-visible external interfaces · 2026-09-27 — USB and power-input peripherals identified; pin schedules remain OPEN.

The SoMakeIt page calls this unit “Elegoo Mars 2P,” while the captured ELEGOO manual explicitly applies to Mars 2 and Mars 2 Pro. The manual’s illustrated component page is labelled Mars 2 Pro, so the local machine’s exact variant remains unresolved.

Sources: SoMakeIt printer-model page; ELEGOO Mars 2/Mars 2 Pro manual, pp. 2, 5–6. Captured manual SHA-256 a80ab63401a56833bb889f04b60014bbe4d9bae8857763a43d88f24581f89afa. The complete source and unresolved identity/contact fields are recorded in the research dossier.

Elegoo Mars 3 4K · manufacturer external interfaces · 2026-09-27 — USB storage and DC input shown as OPEN peripherals; no contacts or routes invented.

The local catalogue labels the machine Mars 3 4K. ELEGOO’s official manual applies to Mars 3 and Mars 3 Pro, so the exact local submodel remains unverified. Its components drawing labels a USB interface and DC Input; the procedure says to export files to a U Disk or SD Card and plug the U Disk into the printer.

Sources: ELEGOO Mars 3 support files and Mars 3/Mars 3 Pro manual, pp. 2, 4–6, 14. Captured manual SHA-256 65ff905bb7472725bf820575fe432de71cc5e26646e7e0d155d5e212d8df6ca2. Full evidence boundary: research dossier.

DeineFraesmaschine · dotted Mach3 STEP/DIR function hypotheses · 2026-09-27 — six user-requested guesses into a hypothetical DB25 peripheral; all other machine paths remain OPEN.

The manufacturer plan identifies Mach3 and page 5's PC_SUB-D connection but provides no PC-to-breakout cavity map or confirmed 25-contact housing. The official Mach3Mill Setup tutorial gives a three-axis example: X STEP/DIR on parallel-port pins 2/3, Y on 4/5 and Z on 6/7. It explicitly says actual machine pinouts may differ. Those six function relationships now appear as dotted violet GUESS lines from SmoothieBox X/Y/Z STEP/DIR contacts to conditional contacts 2–7 on the peripheral card. This follows the requested peripheral layout; it is not an installed pin map or a qualified connection.

Reference: Mach3Mill Setup tutorial release 2.5, pp. 2–3. The tutorial warns that the actual machine pinout may differ. The manufacturer plan and tutorial do not qualify the fitted shell, breakout map, SmoothieBox drive capability, levels, current, timing, polarity, isolation, signal reference, installed cable or safety behavior. The dotted lines are research hypotheses; do not wire from them.

Newly verified positions

The upstream Klipper CR-30 2021 configuration documents an optional direct-serial breakout on the 10-position IDC cable used by the LCD module. The source numbers four positions; they describe that firmware/cable arrangement, not compatibility with SmoothieBox or the positions at a mating-face view. Six positions remain function-unassigned.

Source cable positionDocumented function in optional direct-serial setupSmoothieBox route
1Not specifiedOPEN
2Not specifiedOPEN
3USART3 TxOPEN
4USART3 RxOPEN
5Not specifiedOPEN
6Not specifiedOPEN
7Not specifiedOPEN
8Not specifiedOPEN
9GNDOPEN
10VCC (voltage unspecified by this note)OPEN

Evidence locator: upstream file Klipper3d/klipper/config/printer-creality-cr30-2021.cfg, introductory comment naming the CR-30, STM32F103, optional USART3 serial, and “10 pin IDC” LCD cable mapping (3 Tx, 4 Rx, 9 GND, 10 VCC). This is a firmware/configuration source for a 2021 configuration; it does not prove every CR-30 revision has this cable mapping. No DB25 or external stepper-driver contact map has been established. GUESS routes: none.

Source URL (plain text): https://github.com/Klipper3d/klipper/blob/ce7002bedf37e938bb483572949f3703ac6476cb/config/printer-creality-cr30-2021.cfg
